claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the **name(s) of the child or children** you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know! I'm here to help you assess eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

To begin, could you please tell me **how old Alex is** (or what their date of birth is)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Alex is 9 years old.

Now, are you **Alex's parent or guardian**, and are you the person who would be claiming Child Benefit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm Alex's parent and I would be the one claiming the benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful to know.

Now, I need to ask about your **residency status in the UK**. Are you a UK resident, and if so, what is your current residency situation? (For example, are you a British citizen, settled status, EU citizen, etc.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm a British citizen and live here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information.

Now, are you **currently working or receiving any income**? If so, could you tell me roughly what your annual income is, or whether you receive any specific benefits or allowances?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I do work, yes. Why do you need to know about my income? I thought Child Benefit was available to everyone?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question! Child Benefit is indeed available to most families with children, but there are some circumstances where eligibility can be affected by income. Specifically, there's a High Income Child Benefit Charge that applies if your income exceeds a certain threshold.

However, to give you the most accurate assessment, I do need to understand your income situation. Could you tell me approximately **what your annual income is**? This will help me determine whether any special rules might apply to your claim.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand. My annual income is around £45,000.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. That's helpful.

Just to clarify a couple more details: **Are there any other adults in your household who might also be earning income?** For example, a partner or spouse? If so, do you know their approximate annual income?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have a partner who lives with us. Their income is about £35,000 a year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One more question: **Is Alex living with you full-time, or does Alex spend time with another parent or guardian in a different household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that.

Just one final question to complete my assessment: **Are you or your partner currently receiving any benefits or tax credits** (such as Income Support, Jobseeker's Allowance, Universal Credit, Working Tax Credit, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us are receiving any benefits or tax credits at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the situation:
- You are Alex's parent and UK resident (British citizen in Manchester)
- Alex is 9 years old and lives with you full-time
- Your household income is approximately £80,000 combined (£45,000 + £35,000)
- You're not receiving any benefits or tax credits

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you would be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Your combined household income is below the threshold where the High Income Child Benefit Charge would apply (which currently starts at £60,000 for the highest earner's income). Additionally, you meet all the other key requirements: you're a UK resident, Alex is a qualifying child living with you, and you have responsibility for Alex.

Let me now provide your formal eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Your application meets all the necessary requirements, and there are no barriers to your claim. You should be able to proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit through the UK government's system.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
